summary.headline: Snowman Logistics Q4 FY26 call: West Asia disruption keeps volumes subdued; FY26 double-stack share averaged 40%, Q4 at 42%, with margins pressured by start-up warehouses and domestic ramp-up costs.
summary.overview: Management described volumes as still subdued in Q4 and April due to the West Asia conflict, with import cargo from US, Europe and Middle East and export food cargo hit. Snowman's EBITDA and EBIT per TEU and margins fell year on year and quarter on quarter, which management attributed to start-up warehouses (Kolkata, Krishnapatnam) with high power costs, DG running costs, stabling and empty haulage costs, one-time 5PL import procurement, and domestic ramp-up upfront costs. Management reiterated a INR1,000 crore revenue target for Snowman (15% blended EBITDA margin, about INR150 crore EBITDA) but said it may slip about a year, with FY29 seen as more realistic. Capex guidance for FY27 is about INR50 crore, and gross debt at Gateway is expected to keep declining.

segments.name: Rail (ICD / container rail)
segments.commentary: About 96,000 rail TEUs in Q4; double-stacking averaged 40% in FY26. Management targets about 15% growth for rail as new terminals are added, though FY26 rail throughput grew about 10% per management and about 4.3% CAGR FY22 to FY26 per analyst.

segments.name: CFS
segments.commentary: About 91,000 CFS TEUs in Q4. Management targets about 5% growth. Management said it is not actively looking for a buyer for the CFS business.

segments.name: Snowman Logistics (cold chain warehousing, 5PL, transport)
segments.commentary: Capacity about 160,000 pallets, with the nearest organised competitor at about 80,000 pallets. Warehouse utilisation about 86% to 87% for FY26; dry share about 9% to 10% and being reduced. Management targets about 15% growth and INR1,000 crore revenue at 15% blended EBITDA margin, about INR150 crore EBITDA.

guidance_outlook: Snowman revenue target INR1,000 crore at 15% blended EBITDA margin (about INR150 crore EBITDA); management says it may be deferred by about a year, with FY29 more realistic.
Rail and Snowman growth target about 15% each as terminals are added; CFS growth target about 5%.
FY27 capex guidance about INR50 crore (BTS, one owned warehouse, land, vehicles).

Indore ICD (INR150 crore project, about INR50 crore spent on land) targets operations in 2028; about INR100 crore to be spent over next 2 years. Jaipur ICD adds about INR70 crore if the case resolves.
Tax: MAT rate reduced by 1%; ATI tax benefit lost, so management expects no cash tax for about 3 to 4 years using MAT credit.
Management says it is not looking to increase its stake in Snowman in the near term; dividends are expected to remain part of cash deployment.
capex_capacity: Ankleshwar MMLP (with Sawariya Group) is ramping up domestic volumes month on month and has won an ArcelorMittal steel coil rake handling tender; full ICD operations expected in 3 to 6 months as permissions come through.
Indore ICD: INR150 crore project, about INR50 crore spent on land, remaining INR100 crore over 2 years; target commencement 2028.
Jaipur ICD: final hearing listed for July; if resolved, about INR70 crore spread over 1 to 1.5 years.

Other capex: electric reach stackers (first order placed), three rakes (about INR55 crore), EVs at about INR90 lakh per trailer blended cost, solar, new warehouse; about INR125 crore of additional spend cited.
Yard extensions planned at Garhi and Piyala at about 70% to 80% utilisation; land bank can support up to 4x current ICD volume.
demand_pricing: West Asia conflict continues to subdue volumes; April trend similar to March (within range, not materially worse). Recovery timing unclear and tied to Iran-US resolution.
Warehousing pricing is positive: price increases passed through (including Haryana wage law changes) and management will seek price hikes at each contract renewal.

Snowman market position: about 160,000 pallets capacity versus about 80,000 for the second organised player; Snowman about 3% to 4% of total market including unorganised capacity. Management stopped giving region-wise market share.
Potential LCL and time-sensitive cargo opportunity post DFC: 6,000 to 10,000 TEUs per month within NCR, but nothing happening now and JNPT double-stack operations still pending by a couple of months.
Domestic business is lower-margin on revenue and EBITDA per TEU; management expects overall EBITDA to grow even as per-TEU metrics fall.

qa_highlights.question: Current trend in volumes after West Asia impact, and which commodities are affected?
qa_highlights.answer: Volumes remain subdued with no clarity on recovery. Imports from US, Europe and Middle East and food, rice and frozen exports were hit.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee costs rise about 12% to 13% in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Mix of headcount additions ahead of Ankleshwar and domestic scale-up, plus retention bonuses.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Snowman gross and EBITDA margins fall and COGS rise about 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Start-up warehouse costs (Kolkata, Krishnapatnam), DG power costs, stabling and empty haulage costs, upfront domestic costs, and one-time 5PL import procurement. Management said COGS relates to trading, which grew 23%.

qa_highlights.question: Capex in FY26 and FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Container capex about INR90 crore; Snowman about INR30 crore. FY27 guidance about INR50 crore for BTS, land, one owned warehouse and vehicles.

qa_highlights.question: Lease-related cash outflows and FY27 debt servicing?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 principal repayments about INR30 crore; lease rent about INR40 crore for the year, charged to P&L, with no separate lease principal repayment.

qa_highlights.question: Gross debt trajectory and use of cash flows?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross debt to keep declining; capex plans (rakes, EVs, solar, reach stackers, warehouses, Indore and Jaipur) absorb cash; dividends to continue; no near-term stake increase in Snowman.

qa_highlights.question: Is 15% rail growth achievable given historical 4% to 5% growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said rail grew about 10% last year, exceeding market growth, and cited new ICDs (Ankleshwar, Indore, Jaipur) and domestic volumes as drivers.

qa_highlights.question: Is the transport segment worth keeping versus outsourcing?
qa_highlights.answer: Owns about 250 to 260 vehicles and leases about 200; plans to add vehicles; a transport management system going live within about a month for trip-level profitability tracking.

risks_watch: Prolonged West Asia disruption affecting import and export volumes; April trend similar to March.
Margin recovery: whether start-up warehouse costs, DG costs and empty haulage hits normalise in FY27; management said it is too early to predict.
Snowman INR1,000 crore revenue target could slip to FY29; per-TEU realisations and EBITDA trending lower as domestic mix rises.
Jaipur ICD legal outcome at the July hearing; Indore ICD timeline to 2028.
JNPT DFC last-stretch completion and double-stack readiness; timing of any volume shift still open.
Cash flow visibility: management agreed to consider a cash flow reporting format (lease rentals below EBITDA) from next quarter.
Transport segment remains under stress; TMS rollout to drive lane-level decisions.
Tax: MAT credit to shield cash tax for about 3 to 4 years, but ATI tax benefit lost.
summary.management_tone: Candid and cautious on near-term demand, saying the West Asia trend continues with no clarity on recovery. Confident on long-term plans (15% growth targets, new ICDs, capex), but repeatedly deferred to later timelines and declined to quantify several items such as competition and market share.
key_quotes: So, volumes remain a bit subdued, and there's no clarity also on when things will pick up exactly. So, it's a wait-and-watch kind of situation.
INR1,000 crores is still our plan. Maybe it gets deferred by a year or so.
But maybe more realistic is FY '29.
Yes. For every contract renewal, we are making sure that we ask and pass on the costs, which have increased during the last financial year and expected to increase in the current financial year.

growth.why: Management targets INR1,000 crore Snowman revenue (~15% EBITDA margin) but says it may slip about a year to FY29; Snowman revenue grew ~10% in FY26 and rail/Snowman growth target ~15% vs CFS ~5%, backed mainly by Indore/Jaipur ICD projects, rakes and price pass-throughs, while West Asia keeps volumes subdued into April with no clear recovery date.
